fieldNotes.truckGate: Truck yard, docks and trailer drop lots are wide open directly off the public access road on the east side of the property. Multiple Street View headings (2024-08) along that road show no barrier arm, no sliding/swing gate, and no pinch-point checkpoint where the yard meets the road - the paved truck apron simply abuts the road.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at any truck approach. A metal gantry frame stands in the yard but is a lighting/sign structure, not a guard booth.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because there is no truck gate at all (remoteGs requires a gate without a shack).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Large interconnected manufacturing complex plus a separate building cluster to the NE and on-site wastewater treatment ponds to the west - a campus.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock banks appear on at least two distinct building faces (the north/NE face fronting the main trailer drop yard, and a SW face) - consistent with separate shipping/receiving clusters.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Roughly 30-40 doors estimated across the multiple building faces from z18-z20 imagery; counted indirectly via trailers backed in and dock-bay rhythm - flagged as estimate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Very large drop yards: rows of dozens of parked trailers (white and orange) on the NE lot plus additional rows near the SW dock apron - well over 50.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale clearly visible; flagged as uncertain due to the size and openness of the yard.
fieldNotes.railServed: An active rail line runs along the south edge of the property (parallels Route 104); spur access into the plant is plausible but the line clearly serves/borders the site.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Roster cites ~217 acres for the full parcel including orchard/woods; the developed industrial perimeter measured here is roughly 105 acres.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: The truck approach apron is extremely wide and open with abundant unused paved width - ample room for express/bypass lanes.
